name: Sweden
tagline: Elegant cities, thousands of islands, folk traditions and the northern lights.
cardDescription: A Nordic country of clean, design-led cities, an archipelago of islands, medieval towns, forests and Arctic wilderness.
metaDescription: A complete Sweden travel guide: the 10 best places to visit, from Stockholm and Gothenburg to Gotland, Dalarna and Lapland, with practical tips, a two-week itinerary and costs.

intro: Sweden is a long country in northern Europe, from the Baltic coast and the southern plains to the Arctic mountains of Lapland. It is known for design, clean cities, strong social values and a deep connection to nature, shaped by the right of public access that lets everyone walk, swim and camp in the countryside.

The capital, Stockholm, is spread across islands and has a medieval old town, great museums and an archipelago on its doorstep. Gothenburg and Malmo offer seafood, parks and a relaxed southern atmosphere, while historic towns like Uppsala, Visby and Kalmar show the country's medieval and Viking past.

Further north, Dalarna is the heart of Swedish folk culture, Are is the leading ski resort, and Lapland offers the northern lights, the Midnight Sun and Sami culture. Trains are comfortable and punctual, and English is widely spoken, so Sweden is an easy country to visit.

practicalIntro: The essentials, current for 2026. Sweden is safe and straightforward, but check official sources before travelling.

practical.language: Swedish is the official language. English is widely spoken.
practical.currency: Swedish krona (SEK). Roughly 9-11 kronor to the US dollar in recent years.
practical.money: Sweden is nearly cashless. Cards and phone payments work everywhere.
practical.visa: As a Schengen member, Sweden allows visa-free stays of up to 90 days for many nationalities, but check requirements and ETIAS rules.
practical.plugs: Type C and F, 230 V, 50 Hz.
practical.tipping: Tipping is not required, but rounding up is common in restaurants.
practical.safety: Sweden is very safe. Take normal precautions in cities and prepare well for cold weather and hiking in the north.
practical.connectivity: Excellent. 5G is common and public Wi-Fi is widespread.
practical.timeZone: Central European Time (UTC+1), with daylight saving in summer.

culture.intro: Swedes are polite, reserved and egalitarian, with a love of fairness, punctuality and quiet. The concept of lagom, meaning just enough, shapes life.
dos: Follow the right of public access rules

tips: Book long-distance trains early for cheaper fares.

Cycle helmets are required for children.
